summary: This is a Dev Container configuration file that sets up a reproducible development environment for a Quarto documentation project. It specifies the Docker container to use, installs helpful tools like Git and Docker, configures VS Code settings for consistent code formatting and linting across the team, and installs useful extensions to improve developer workflow.

explanations.3: This tells Dev Containers which Docker Compose file to use to build the container—in this case, a file named compose.yaml in the same directory.
explanations.8: This passes the path of your local project folder into the container as an environment variable, so scripts inside the container can reference where your code is.
explanations.11: This feature gives the container the ability to run Docker commands from inside itself, and the settings allow non-root users to use Docker without needing elevated permissions.
explanations.19: Before the container starts, this command creates a directory structure for bash history and a .gitignore file so your command history persists between container restarts but doesn't clutter your repo.
explanations.20: After you connect to the container, this checks if a pre-commit tool is installed and sets it up; the 'true' at the end means it won't fail if pre-commit isn't available.
explanations.21: These port numbers are forwarded from the container to your computer, so web apps running on ports 8000 or 5931 inside the container are accessible from your browser.
explanations.47: This tells the spell checker to recognize words in English, French, and Dutch so it doesn't flag those language words as misspellings.
explanations.72: This tells VS Code to treat all .json files inside the 'resources' folder as JSONC (JSON with Comments), which is a superset of JSON that allows comments.
explanations.78: The 'exclude' section hides certain folders and files from the file explorer on the left, reducing clutter from build artifacts and cache directories.
explanations.113: This maps URLs to schema definitions, so VS Code can provide autocomplete and validation for Quarto config files and GitHub workflow files based on their official schemas.
